title: Consideration of Matters regarding Member of Parliament, and Suspension of Member
what_it_is: Consideration of Matters regarding Member of Parliament, and Suspension of Member

sections.label: Business Motion amendment disallowed
sections.summary: The Speaker will disallow amendments that substantially qualify, transpose, contradict or nullify the other Motion, as the Business Motion intends debate and a single vote.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As the intent of the Business Motion is for Parliament to debate the two Motions together and vote on them at the end of the debate, I will disallow any amendment that has the effect of substantially qualifying, transposing, contradicting or nullifying the other Motion.

sections.label: Iswaran MP allowance status quo
sections.summary: Agreeing with the Motion and rejecting the PSP Motion maintains the status quo, with Minister Iswaran receiving over $16,000 monthly in MP allowances until CPIB completes its investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If Parliament were to choose to agree with that Motion and to reject the Motion from the PSP, then what is, in fact, happening is that we are maintaining the status quo; which means that Minister Iswaran, during this period of investigation when he is on leave, he will continue to receive more than $16,000 every month in terms of Member of Parliament’s (MP) subsidies or allowance until the Corrupt Practices Investigation Bureau (CPIB) has completed the investigation into him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This means that the annual payout could be up to S$192,500 in terms of MP allowances and it comes from the public coffers, and it is the taxpayers who are actually contributing to the public coffers.

sections.label: PSP urges back pay motion
sections.summary: The PSP urges Parliament to agree to the Motion by Ms Hazel Poa and the speaker, and amend the 1962 Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act to allow back pay for Minister Iswaran.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The PSP would also like to urge Parliament to move or agree to the Motion tabled by Ms Hazel Poa and myself, and amend the 1962 Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act in order to ensure that Parliament has the right to back pay Minister Iswaran while he is absolved and when he resumes his public duties.

sections.label: Two key issues for Parliament
sections.summary: The speaker identifies two key issues: whether suspending an elected MP before due process is fair, and what Parliament should do when an MP is interdicted by a Party leader.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In my view, there are two key issues for Parliament to consider: first, whether it is fair and proper for a duly elected Member of Parliament (MP) to be suspended from responsibilities towards his or her constituents and legislative duties before due process is concluded; second, what Parliament ought to do when an MP has been effectively interdicted from MP duties arising from actions taken by his or her Party leader.

sections.label: WP disagrees with PSP Motion
sections.summary: The WP cannot agree to the Motion filed by the PSP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP cannot agree to the Motion filed by the PSP.

sections.label: Suspend MP allowance not MP
sections.summary: While suspending Mr Iswaran from Parliament may not be appropriate, suspending the payment of his MP allowance may well be appropriate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While it may not be appropriate to suspend Mr Iswaran from Parliament, it may well be appropriate to suspend the payment of his MP allowance.

sections.label: Clawback of MP allowance
sections.summary: A Member asks whether clawing back Mr S Iswaran's MP allowance for the period he did not perform MP duties is contemplated under the Leader's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would advance that such a clawback for the period during which he has not performed MP's duties would be a reasonable expectation of the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my second question is this: can the Leader tell us whether a clawback of Mr S Iswaran's MP allowance is within the PAP's contemplation in so far as clause (c) of the Leader's Motion is concerned?

sections.label: Motion to suspend Iswaran
sections.summary: The Motion asked that Mr S Iswaran be suspended from Parliament for the remainder of the current session of the Fourteenth Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In their Motion, they asked that "This House suspends Mr S Iswaran from the service of Parliament for the remainder of the current session of the Fourteenth Parliament." In Ms Hazel Poa’s Facebook page, she said that she had filed the Motion so that Mr S Iswaran no longer receives his MP allowance while he has been requested by the Prime Minister to not perform any official duties during his investigation by CPIB.

sections.label: Prime Minister's CPIB statement
sections.summary: Prime Minister Lee stated on 2 August 2023 that CPIB came across information concerning Minister Iswaran while investigating a separate matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In the statement made by the Prime Minister on 2 August 2023, Prime Minister Lee said that "while investigating a separate matter, CPIB came across some information concerning Minister Iswaran that merited investigation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Minister Iswaran was brought in by CPIB and subsequently released on bail.

sections.label: Support for Leader's Motion
sections.summary: The speaker opposes Ms Poa and Mr Leong's Motion and supports the Leader's Motion to wait for the investigations' outcome before considering other action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Is it their position that you punish first – suspend, cut his salary – and then reimburse him later if he is found guilty?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, for that reason, I cannot support this Motion by Ms Poa and Mr Leong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I firmly believe that once the case against Mr Iswaran is concluded, the Government will do whatever is right to ensure that all parties are treated fairly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, I support the Motion by the Leader of the House that we wait for the outcome of the investigations before considering any other action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The reimbursement should be if the Member is found innocent.

sections.label: Circumstances vacating MP seat
sections.summary: Article 46(2) enumerates circumstances in which an MP's seat becomes vacant, including resignation, absence from Sittings and disqualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The MP's seat would only become vacant under certain circumstances, which are enumerated in article 46(2).

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These include: (a) resigning; (b) failing to attend Sittings in two consecutive months without obtaining leave from the Speaker; and (c) becoming subject to the disqualifications from being a Member of Parliament like being convicted for an offence by a Court and sentenced to imprisonment for a term of not less than one year or to a fine of not less than $10,000.

sections.label: Presumption of innocence and suspension
sections.summary: The speaker says the presumption of innocence stands and suspending the Minister as an MP is premature, with no mechanism to suspend only an MP's salary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the current matter, the presumption of innocence continues to stand unrebutted and any move by Parliament to suspend the Minister as an MP is not only premature but does not have legal legs to stand on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For completeness, there is also no mechanism to suspend merely an MP's salary.

sections.label: MPs standards and investigations
sections.summary: The Motion restates standards for MPs, affirms fair but firm treatment after investigations start, and resolves to act once outcomes are known.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Her Motion restates the standards that we expect our MPs to have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It affirms that they are to be treated fairly but firmly in the period after investigations are initiated, but before the presumption of innocence is rebutted, and resolves to deal with the matter at hand once the outcomes of investigations are known.

sections.label: Poa and presumption of innocence
sections.summary: Ms Poa glossed over the basic requirement for suspension, that the presumption of innocence must first be rebutted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, Ms Poa even glossed over the basic requirement to invoke any of the avenues for suspension, which is that the presumption of innocence must first be rebutted.

sections.label: Public concern and due process
sections.summary: Public concern indicates Government should address matters and assure the public, but due process must run its course during investigations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where there is public concern and emotion on certain matters, it is an indication to our Government to address these matters and to assure the public, which is what the Prime Minister and other Ministers had done in relation to this matter at the last Sitting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As much as I can understand public frustration with having to wait while investigations are underway, we must allow due process to run its course.

sections.label: Support for Minister Indranee
sections.summary: The speaker will not support the NCMPs' Motion and will support Minister Indranee's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the reasons I had set out in my speech, I will not support the Motion raised by the hon NCMPs, and I will support that raised by Minister Indranee.

sections.label: Provisions for suspending Members
sections.summary: PIPPA and the Standing Orders allow suspension of a Member's rights for dishonourable conduct, abuse of privilege, or contempt of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There are clear provisions, Mr Speaker, that allow Member's rights to be suspended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These are set out in the Parliament (Privileges, Immunities and Powers) Act 1962, which I will refer to as PIPPA for short, and the SOs of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Section 20 of PIPPA sets out the punitive powers of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These punitive powers include, under section 20C, the powers to suspend a Member.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These powers can only be exercised where a Member has engaged in: one, dishonourable conduct; two, abused privilege; or three, engaged in contempt of Parliament.

sections.label: Retrospective liability and suspension
sections.summary: The speaker disagrees with the amendments, citing retrospective criminal liability, and says there is not enough information to suspend Mr Iswaran.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Additionally, if this legislation is meant to apply to Mr Iswaran for conduct he had engaged in prior to the legislation coming into place, this would also be a breach to the principle that legislation should not impose criminal liability retrospectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For this reason, I also do not agree with the proposed amendments to the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, in brief, Mr Speaker, I agree with the Leader of the House that, at this time, we do not have enough information to make a decision to suspend Mr Iswaran and none of the clear provisions for suspension set out in both PPIPA and the SOs apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I also disagree with the Motion put forward by Ms Hazel Poa because I believe that the powers of suspension should be exercised only in accordance with the express requirements of PPIPA and the SOs.

sections.label: Suspension pay and dishonourable conduct
sections.summary: Section 29(3) says suspended Members are not paid, while section 20 allows suspension for dishonourable conduct, abuse of privilege or contempt.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Section 29(3) of the PPIPA says, "no salary or allowance payable to such Member for his service as a Member of Parliament shall be paid in respect of any period during which he is suspended from service in Parliament." So, section 29(3) is the provision that says that if you are suspended, then you do not get your pay.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Well, there is a specific provision in section 20, which says that "for any dishonourable conduct, abuse of privilege or contempt on the part of a Member, Parliament may" – and then, it has various things – "may suspend him from the service of Parliament for the remainder of the current session of Parliament or for any part thereof." So, there is one specific provision which has a certain threshold with three requirements: dishonourable conduct, abuse of privilege or contempt.

sections.label: SO59(1) suspension procedure
sections.summary: SO59(1) lets a Minister move forthwith to suspend a Member named for disregarding the Chair or obstructing business, with no debate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: SO59, subsection (1) has a specific provision on suspension.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It states: "Whenever a Member has been named by the Speaker or the Chairman immediately after the commission of the offence of disregarding the authority of the Chair, or of persistently and wilfully obstructing the business of Parliament by abusing the rules of Parliament or otherwise, then if the offence has been committed by such Member of Parliament, a motion shall forthwith be proposed by a Minister or Parliamentary Secretary present that the Member shall be suspended from the service of Parliament and the Speaker shall forthwith put the question on that motion, no amendment, adjournment or debate being allowed".

sections.label: SO59(5) general suspension resolution
sections.summary: SO59(5) is a general provision stating Parliament can move a resolution to suspend, raising a question of principle.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But SO59(5) is a general provision which just basically says that Parliament can move a resolution.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if you are relying on that provision, effectively what you are saying is that "because I can pass a Motion to suspend you, I will." That is where the question of principle comes in.

sections.label: Iswaran asked to take leave
sections.summary: Mr Iswaran was asked to take leave of absence because performing his Minister and MP duties while under investigation was untenable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is the reason why you have to take leave of absence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And in this case, Mr Iswaran was effectively asked to take leave of absence because it is untenable for him to perform his duties as a Minister and it will be very difficult for him to perform his duties as an MP whilst under investigation.

sections.label: Wait for investigation outcome
sections.summary: The Motion says Parliament should wait for the investigations' outcome because the threshold has not yet been met.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It may well be, depending on the outcome of the investigations, that that threshold may be crossed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, that is why my Motion at this point in time says that we should wait until the outcome of the investigations before deciding what to do, simply because that threshold has not yet been met.

sections.label: Waiting for proceedings outcome
sections.summary: In the Committee of Privileges referrals for Mr Singh and Mr Faisal Manap, they said they would wait for the proceedings' outcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In the case of the referral to the Public Prosecutor on the Committee of Privileges Inquiry for Mr Singh and Mr Faisal Manap, we actually said that we would wait till the outcome of the proceedings.

sections.label: Referral to Public Prosecutor
sections.summary: The committee recommends Parliament refer Mr Singh's conduct to the Public Prosecutor and defer action on dishonourable conduct and contempt until criminal proceedings end.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: However, we recommend that Parliament refers Mr Singh's conduct to the Public Prosecutor, with a view to consider the institution of criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We would also recommend that Parliament consider deferring any action to be taken in respect of possible dishonourable conduct and contempt of Parliament until criminal proceedings, if any, are complete." The point I want to make is this.

sections.label: No Suspension of Allowance
sections.summary: The PPIPA has no provision to suspend allowance, so a sitting MP receives the full allowance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The difficulty with that, and this is what Ms Poa was alluding to, is that there is no provision in the PPIPA currently to suspend allowance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is a binary position: if the person is a sitting MP, he receives the full allowance.

sections.label: Prime Minister Considers Charges
sections.summary: If charged, the Prime Minister will consider the allegations and decide whether to make him resign and repay salary and allowance before legal process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If he is charged, the Prime Minister will consider the allegations and accusations against him and decide whether to make him resign and to pay back both salary and allowance without waiting for legal process.

sections.label: Considering Claw Back
sections.summary: What exactly will be done depends on what happens, but a claw back will certainly be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As to what exactly we will have to do, we will have to see what happens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But I have said quite plainly that we will certainly consider a claw back and also think how to do it.

sections.label: Expulsion Grounds in PPIPA
sections.summary: Sections 19 and 20 of PPIPA and SO59 set out expulsion grounds, otherwise the PPIPA suspension provisions would be irrelevant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I do not know whether they have taken legal advice or whether they have read the provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But sections 19 and 20 of PPIPA set out the grounds for expulsion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: SO59, subsections (1) to (4) set out the grounds on which there can be expulsion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If you are right, then all the carefully drafted provisions in PPIPA setting out when exactly Parliament can suspend an MP are irrelevant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs and Law (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Because whenever Parliament does not like someone, we can pass a resolution by majority and throw the person out or suspend that person.

sections.label: Amendment Bill for Allowances
sections.summary: Leave was sought to table an amendment Bill to let Parliament back pay Minister Iswaran, since suspended Members get no allowances under the PPIPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: That is a judgement call and I think we will have to agree to disagree.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I have also asked for leave to table an amendment Bill to make it possible for Parliament to back pay Minister Iswaran, if necessary.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under current provisions in the PPIPA, no allowances are to be paid to Members who are suspended from the service of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We have proposed to amend that provision to allow Parliament to pay such allowances if a resolution is passed.

sections.label: Minister pay versus ComCare
sections.summary: The passage asks what it says about values that Minister Iswaran receives over $20,000 monthly while under investigation, compared with ComCare recipients getting $640 monthly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If Minister Iswaran continues to receive over $20,000 per month while not performing any duties and under investigation for corruption, while ComCare recipients who are permanently unable to work due to old age, illness or disability get $640 per month, what does this say about our values?

sections.label: Minister and MP roles
sections.summary: The passage states it is important to remember there is a distinction between Mr Iswaran's role as a Minister and his role as an MP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, it is important to remember that there is a distinction between Mr Iswaran's role as a Minister and his role as an MP.

sections.label: Interdiction and building access
sections.summary: The passage states the interdiction includes a direction that he should not be allowed access to all Government buildings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: That is as I understand it and if I am incorrect, my colleagues will set out the correct position.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But that interdiction includes a direction that he should not be allowed access to all Government buildings.

sections.label: MP mandate and party discipline
sections.summary: The passage states his mandate comes from voters, only the PPIPA can suspend his MP role, and the Prime Minister requested he cease MP duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: His mandate comes from them, and you can only suspend or take away his ability to act as an MP in accordance with the PPIPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, in other words, currently, because he is not suspended, if Mr Iswaran wanted to come today and enter Parliament, he can because he is an MP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But as a matter of party discipline, he has been requested by the Prime Minister to also cease his MP duties because you can imagine how difficult it is to carry out your MP duties when you are under investigation or even to come to Parliament.

sections.label: Possible clawback consideration
sections.summary: The passage states that if a certain threshold has been met and it was warranted, a clawback would be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Well, as I said earlier, if a certain threshold has been met, if it was warranted, then we would consider having a clawback.

sections.label: Wait for investigation outcome
sections.summary: The passage states that if Mr Iswaran acceded, nothing more need be done, and any amending Bill depends on the investigation outcome.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And if Mr Iswaran acceded to that, then there is actually nothing more to be done, if it warranted it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, to ask me now, can I confirm that we will have a Bill or something to amend – my answer is, wait and see what the outcome of the investigation is because such a Bill may not be necessary.

sections.label: MP integrity and Iswaran investigation
sections.summary: The House affirms that MPs must uphold integrity and be dealt with firmly and fairly, and resolves to consider MP S Iswaran's matter when investigations end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The question is, "That this House: (a) Affirms the need for Members of Parliament to uphold the highest standards of integrity and conduct themselves in accordance with the law; (b) Affirms the need to deal firmly and fairly with any Member of Parliament who is being investigated for possible wrongdoing; and (c) Resolves to consider the matter regarding Member of Parliament S Iswaran when the outcome of the ongoing investigations against him is known." As many as are of that opinion say "Aye".

sections.label: Suspending MP S Iswaran
sections.summary: The question proposes that the House suspend Mr S Iswaran from the service of Parliament for the remainder of the current session of the 14th Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The question is, "That this House suspends Mr S Iswaran from the service of Parliament for the remainder of the current session of the 14th Parliament." As many as are of that opinion say "Aye".
